# Feature: Agent Grounding — User-Granted Context, No Guessed URLs, Real Form Filling

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-007
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Stop the agent from inventing the two facts a web task most depends on — **who the user is (location)** and **where a page lives (URL)** — by making sensitive ambient context an explicit, user-granted input, and by giving the agent a tool that can actually drive a multi-field search form so it stops falling back to inventing them.

### Evidence: run `20260803T033803Z-do-f1d9f01b`

Goal: _"cheap hotels near me August 5 2026 2 nights"_. The run reported `completed` with no failure recorded. Three defects produced a plausible-looking but ungrounded answer.

**① Location was inferred from the timezone.** Agent thinking, turn 6:

> _"The timezone is America/Chicago, which covers a large area... let me use a general location like 'Chicago' since the timezone is America/Chicago. That would be a reasonable interpretation."_

Published in the Brief: _"Since your exact location wasn't provided, I used Chicago, IL based on your America/Chicago timezone."_ Two causes: `ambientLines` supplies a timezone and nothing else, and the interaction line explicitly instructs the model to "pick the most reasonable interpretation and complete it." `locale.region` already exists in `profile.yaml` and reaches the LLM through `buildPersonalizationContext`, but only `ask` passes it — `do` and `research` send no `profileContext` at all.

**② A hand-built URL silently returned a different city.** Turn 18:

```
https://www.kayak.com/hotels/Chicago,IL-c17823/2026-08-05/2026-08-07/1adults;map?sort=price_a
```

`c17823` is a fabricated Kayak city id. The page returned **"Shook, Missouri, United States"** — eight cabins at Lake Wappapello. `browser_navigate` returned `status: ok`; nothing flagged it. The agent then hand-built a second deep link for hotels.com and published from it.

**③ The form failure caused ②.** After filling the destination combobox (`e14`), the agent clicked `e38` believing it was an autocomplete suggestion. `e38` was a marketing tile: _"View more deals for Chicago Hotels."_ The real suggestions never appeared, for two compounding reasons:

- `scanInteractablesInPage` does not select `[role="option"]` at all, so autocomplete options are **structurally invisible** to every observation.
- Even if they were scanned, `rankInteractables` caps at 30 by viewport position; header links and calendar cells win.

The check-in/check-out fields are `role: button` that open a calendar widget, not fillable inputs. The agent never solved dates on kayak, gave up, and guessed the URL — its turn-18 thinking says so directly: _"let me try to navigate to a URL with the search parameters already set."_

## 2. Technical Context

Standing rules live in `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

Four layers, each independently testable:

1. **Location becomes user-granted data**, not a model inference. A new `context` block in `profile.yaml` records which sensitive facts the user permits — today just `location`; `yantra init` asks for it; `locale.city` supplies the value. Date, timezone, and locale stay unconditional. Location renders on **every** run — as a value, or as an explicit `not available` marker paired with an instruction never to derive it.
2. **A deterministic pre-flight gate** refuses goals that need a location when none is available, before any tokens are spent or a browser launches. It reuses the existing `handoff` outcome (exit 4) and tailors its remedy to whether the grant was denied or the value was never set.
3. **A run-scoped URL provenance allowlist** restricts `browser_navigate` to URLs a tool result actually produced. Built as a sibling of the existing `EvidenceLedger`.
4. **`browser_form_fill`** fills an ordered list of fields, re-observing the live page against the **uncapped** interactable scan between every step, so elements revealed by the previous step (autocomplete options, calendar cells) become addressable.

Prompt text changes are surgical. `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is pinned to five governed sections (`plan_agentic.md` §6), so no section is added — the existing **Trust boundary** sentence, which already forbids inventing things, is extended to cover both ① and ②.

### Design Decisions

**Only location is grantable; date and locale always render.** The current date, timezone, and locale tag are host-environment facts, not personal data, so they stay unconditional as they are today. Making `date` deniable would have re-opened the exact failure the ambient block exists to prevent — small models guessing the current date from their training prior. Location is the one genuinely sensitive value and the only one the user chooses about. The `context` block is nonetheless introduced as a **block**, not a lone flag, so a future sensitive fact is a one-line addition rather than a schema reshape.

**Denied and unconfigured render identically to the model.** Both become `not available`. The model's correct behavior is the same in each case (don't have it, don't derive it, blocker if the goal needs it), and distinguishing them would leak that the user holds a value they are withholding while giving the model nothing actionable. The **user-facing** remedy does distinguish them — the location gate reads the grant directly and prints either "set `locale.city`" or "re-enable `context.location`".

**The pre-flight gate stays location-only.** "Needs a location" has a small, matchable phrase set. "Needs the date" is true of nearly every goal and has no clean deterministic test, so `date` and `locale` rely on the marker and the prompt rule instead.

**`init` prompts are TTY-gated.** `init.ts` is documented as _"a minimal non-interactive init suitable for CI and scripted use."_ Prompts fire only on an interactive TTY without `--json`/`--yes`, and only when the profile is actually being written (absent, or `--reset`), so scripted use and re-runs are unaffected.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

**Override 1 — user location goes in the ambient block.** `prompt.ts:47-52` currently documents the opposite:

> _"Values are engine-owned (clock and host environment), never user or model input, so they bypass the sanitizer. User-specific facts such as location belong in the approved profile context."_

The ambient block is the right home: the profile-context block is optional and absent on `do`/`research`, which is exactly why the failure occurred. The safety property that comment protected is preserved by attaching it to the value instead of the location — `resolveUserLocation` returns `Sanitized<string>`, so the brand enforces sanitization at the type level and `AgentAmbientContext` cannot accept an unsanitized location. TASK-004 corrects the comment.

**Override 2 — `personalization.ts` is no longer the only preference→prompt path.** Its module doc claims to be _"the ONLY code path that turns a user's preferences into text bound for an LLM prompt"_ and lists three structural guarantees. `resolveUserLocation` becomes a second such path and therefore upholds all three: it accepts **only** `EffectivePreferences` (so raw history structurally cannot enter — the existing privacy property test's invariant is preserved by construction), reads **only approved** rows, and returns a **sanitized, length-capped, branded** value. TASK-001 amends the doc to describe two chokepoints under one rule set and adds the matching compile guard.

**Override 3 — `browser_form_fill` does not accept `secret_ref`.** `browser_fill` remains the only credentialed fill path, so `assertHostBinding`, `withSecret`, and the consent flow are untouched by this feature. The new tool takes plain strings only and still runs the `SECRET_SHAPE` guard on every value.

### Deliberate Scope Exclusions

Stated explicitly so they are not mistaken for oversights:

- **`web_fetch` is not provenance-gated.** It carries the same guess-a-URL risk, but following a URL quoted in page text is a legitimate `ask`/`research` flow and page text is not in provenance. Gating it needs its own design → TODO.
- **The model-visible 30-interactable cap is unchanged.** `browser_form_fill` resolves against the uncapped scan internally, so raising the cap would spend model context to solve a problem the tool already solves → TODO.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No relational schema. Two additions to the `profile.yaml` document schema (`packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts`), which is `.strict()` — an unknown key is a validation error, so the schema must be extended before either key is usable.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`ProfileFile.context`** — **NEW block**. The user's grants over sensitive ambient facts. Uniform booleans so a future fact is a one-line addition.
  - `location` (`boolean`, default `true`) — permits rendering the value composed from `locale.city` / `locale.region`. Default `true` is behavior-preserving: with no city configured the block still renders `not available`, so an untouched install behaves exactly as it does today.
  - _(Date, timezone, and locale are host-environment facts and deliberately **not** grants — they always render. See Design Decisions.)_

- **`ProfileFile.locale`** (existing block):
  - `city` (`string | null`, default `null`) — **NEW**. Free text at city grain, e.g. `"Naperville, IL"`. Trimmed, min length 1 when present.
  - `region` (`string | null`, default `null`) — existing, unchanged. Country/region grain.
  - `units` (`'metric' | 'imperial'`) — existing, unchanged.

### Relationships

- `context.location` **gates** the pair (`locale.city`, `locale.region`). Granted + at least one value → composed string. Granted + neither value → `null`. Denied → `null` regardless of stored values.
- Composition: both → `"Naperville, IL, US"`; city only → `"Naperville, IL"`; region only → `"US"`.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `'context.location'` and `'locale.city'` must be added to `KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS` so `yantra prefs set|approve` and `yantra profile` accept them.
- Approved-only: both resolvers read a value only when its `EffectivePreference.approved` flag is true, matching `buildPersonalizationContext`.
- Backward compatibility: every new leaf has a Zod default and `context` has `.default({})`, so a `profile.yaml` written before this change loads unchanged with grants defaulted. No migration.
- `resolveUserLocation` caps its output at **120 chars** and returns `Sanitized<string> | null`.

### TASK-008: `browser_form_fill` drives a multi-field form in one call

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `browser-form-fill.ts`. Params (closed, `additionalProperties: false`): `fields` — array, 1..10, of `{ field: string (1..200), value: string (≤4096), pick_suggestion?: boolean }`. `value` is a **plain string only** — no `secret_ref` union (Override 3); the description points credentials at `browser_fill`, and the `SECRET_SHAPE` guard from `browser-fill.ts` runs on every value, returning `SECRET_SHAPED_LITERAL`. Spec flags: `mutating: true`, `sanitizationProfile: 'authenticated'`, no `requiresConfirmation` (the tool never submits). Per field, in order: resolve via the TASK-007 helper against a **fresh uncapped** observation, then dispatch on the resolved role —
  - `textbox` / `searchbox` → `controller.fill(ref, value)`.
  - `combobox` → `controller.fill(ref, value)`; a native `<select>` already routes through `fillSelect`, so `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` surfaces unchanged.
  - `button` (**widget path**, e.g. kayak's date fields) → click the ref, re-observe uncapped, click the element whose name matches `value`. Match exact name first; if `value` parses as an ISO date, also try `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {month:'long', day:'numeric', year:'numeric'})` (kayak renders `"August 5, 2026"`) and a loose match requiring both the month name and the day number. No match → `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` naming the value and listing candidates.
  - `checkbox` / `radio` → `FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_ROLE` pointing at `browser_click`. Out of scope for v1 by design; `browser_click` handles them correctly today.

  When `pick_suggestion` is true, after the fill poll the uncapped observation every 250 ms up to `SUGGESTION_WAIT_MS = 3000` for a `role: 'option'` element, click the best name match against `value`, and return `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED` if none appears in the window. After each field, verify the action took effect (the resolved element's value/state changed, or the option was clicked) and fail the step if it did not. **Stop at the first failing field** — return the fields applied so far plus the typed failure; never continue past a failure and never substitute a guess. Append trace entries exactly as `browser-fill.ts`/`browser-click.ts` do (`safeLocatorFor` + `toCandidateChain`, masking values via `services.userInput?.mask`) so `--save-as` promotion keeps working. Return the post-fill observation (`url`, `title`, `digest`, `interactables`) plus a per-field `applied` summary, so the agent can see the submit button and click it with `browser_click`.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A kayak-shaped fixture — text field + `pick_suggestion` combobox + two calendar buttons — fills end to end and returns an observation containing the submit button. `pick_suggestion` clicks the matching `role: 'option'` and not a same-named marketing tile (**the exact `e38` confusion from the logged run**). `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED` when no option appears within the window. Widget path matches `"August 5, 2026"` from `value: "2026-08-05"`. Ambiguous and not-found field names return their typed errors. A failing second field leaves the first applied and reports the failure. A credential-shaped value is refused. An object-shaped `value` fails schema validation. Trace entries are appended per applied field with values masked. Roles `checkbox`/`radio` return `FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_ROLE`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Tool reference entry — when to use it (multi-field search forms, autocomplete destinations, calendar date fields), when not to (single field → `browser_fill`; credentials → `browser_fill`; submitting → `browser_click`).
- **Verify**: On the kayak hotels page, one `browser_form_fill` call sets destination + both dates and returns an observation whose interactables include the Search button.
- **Depends on**: TASK-007

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: Unchanged. `browser_form_fill` cannot resolve secrets, so `assertHostBinding`, `withSecret`, and the consent gateway keep `browser_fill` as their sole entry point. No new confirmation surface — the tool never submits, which is why the protected-action path (`PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` on "submit"/"book"/"buy") is untouched.
- **Privacy**: The `context` block is the user's control surface over what the engine tells the model about them — today one grant (`location`), collected explicitly at `init` and changeable at any time via `yantra prefs`. Date, timezone, and locale are host-environment facts and stay unconditional. `resolveUserLocation` enforces approved-only reads, sanitization, a 120-char cap, and the `Sanitized` brand, so the ambient block cannot carry an unvetted user value (Override 1). A denied grant is indistinguishable from an unset value in the prompt, so the model cannot infer that a withheld value exists (Design Decisions).
- **Error Handling**: Every new failure is a typed, retryable-classified `DomainFailure` with a stable code and a remedy the agent can act on: `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE` (retryable — search or click instead), `FORM_FIELD_NOT_FOUND` / `FORM_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS` / `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` / `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED` / `FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_ROLE` (retryable — all name the field and list candidates). The location gate is not a tool error but a run-level `handoff` carrying `blocker` + `safestNextAction`, exiting 4 per the documented contract. No path silently degrades: a refused navigation is refused, not rewritten; a form step that cannot be verified fails rather than continuing.
- **Logging**: Provenance refusals go to `tool-calls.jsonl` through the existing recorder, with the offending URL preserved by the existing `UrlAuditSink` (which already audits rejections in full). `browser_form_fill` records one lifecycle entry for the call; per-field detail rides in the sanitized result. Values stay masked through `services.userInput?.mask` in traces, matching `browser-fill.ts`. The resolved location is never logged separately — it appears only in the per-run prompt, whose hash is already recorded in the manifest.

## 9. Implementation Deviations

Recorded at implementation time. Each states what the spec said, what was built, and why.

**DEVIATION 1 — test files use `.spec.ts`, not `.test.ts`.** The spec's Files section names
`*.test.ts`. Every package's `vitest.config.ts` includes only `tests/**/*.spec.ts`, so those files
would have been collected by nothing and the suites would have silently never run. All new tests use
`.spec.ts`, matching the existing convention.

**DEVIATION 2 — two new preference keys, not four.** The Files section says "four new
`KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS`", but the Data Model and TASK-001 both define exactly two leaves
(`context.location`, `locale.city`). Two were added; there is no third and fourth key to add.

**DEVIATION 3 — `--allow-host` grants the whole host, not just its origin root.** TASK-005 says to
seed each `--allow-host` entry as `https://<host>/`. Implemented and then corrected: that rule
(a) never matches at all on an `http` or non-default-port host, because the seeded `https://host/`
shares no origin with `http://host:8931/...`, and (b) refuses the first navigation of an ordinary
`--allow-host` run, since a deep path is not the origin root. Five pre-existing e2e scenarios failed
on exactly this. `UrlProvenance.allowHost()` now grants a user-named host in full (any path, scheme,
port). This is narrowly scoped to hosts the **user** named: a host reached organically mid-run still
gets only exact-URL and origin-root matching, so the logged `c17823` failure — a fabricated path on a
host the user never allowlisted — remains refused. Tests cover the lookalike-host cases
(`notexample.com`, `example.com.evil.com`).

**DEVIATION 4 — a sanitizer bug had to be fixed for TASK-008 to work.** TASK-008 mandates
`sanitizationProfile: 'authenticated'`, whose `stripQueryStrings` fallback ran `/\?([^#\s]+)/g` over
arbitrary text — from any `?` to the next whitespace. `browser_form_fill` returns interactable names,
and a field named `"Where to?"` made the stripper eat straight through the JSON: two entries fused
into one with the intervening keys destroyed. The stop set now also excludes quotes, angle brackets,
and backslashes, which cannot appear unencoded in a real query string, so no genuine stripping is
lost. This is the root cause of the already-filed TODO about mangled `tool-calls.jsonl` URLs.
Regression tests added in `packages/core/tests/sanitizer/strippers.spec.ts`.

**DEVIATION 5 — per-field verification is operation-based, not value-readback.** TASK-008 says to
verify "the resolved element's value/state changed". The observation API deliberately exposes no
element values (a password field's value must never reach the tool layer), so reading one back would
be a privacy regression. Verification is therefore: the controller operation completed without an
actionability/stale error, and every click-path target was actually located and clicked (a missing
option or calendar day is a typed failure). A step that cannot be confirmed this way still fails
rather than continuing.

**DEVIATION 6 — `init` asks one question, not three.** TASK-002's Verify line says `yantra init
--reset` "asks three questions", contradicting its own Implementation text, which specifies one
question plus a chained city prompt. The Implementation text was followed.

**DEVIATION 7 — `isDomainFailure` was generalized.** It was pinned to
`AgentBrowserController | DomainFailure`; the form tool narrows other unions (a resolved field, a
per-field outcome) with the same check. Now generic over `T | DomainFailure`; the runtime check is
unchanged.

**ADDITION — `ambient-context.ts` added to the import-graph guard.** Override 2 states the new
resolver upholds all three personalization privacy properties, the third of which is the build-time
import-graph guard. It is now listed in `DEFAULT_LLM_PAYLOAD_ENTRIES` in `scripts/ci-static-check.ts`.

**ADDITION — `agent-v6` added to the protocol manifest enum.** `prompt_version` is a closed Zod enum
(`packages/protocol/src/schemas/agent-manifest.ts`). Without adding `agent-v6`, every agentic run's
manifest would have failed validation at `RunRecorder.open`. Not mentioned in the spec; found by the
test suite.
